chunks: Those are the apostles; We have favoured some of them over others. Among them were those to whom Allah spoke, and He raised some of them in degrees. And We gave Jesus, son of Mary, clear proofs, and supported him with the Holy Spirit. And if Allah had willed, those who came after them would not have fought one another after the clear proofs had come to them. But they differed, so among them were those who believed, and among them were those who disbelieved. And if Allah had willed, they would not have fought, but Allah does what He intends.
ai.seo_question: How does the Quran explain the differences in status among Prophets and the cause of human conflict?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse establishes the principle of *Fadl* (superiority) among Prophets, distinguishing between those granted direct speech (*Kalimullah*) and those elevated in spiritual rank, while affirming Jesus’ unique support by the *Ruh al-Qudus* (often identified as Gabriel or the Holy Spirit). It contextualizes human conflict not as a failure of divine guidance, but as a consequence of free will despite the arrival of clear proofs (*Bayinat*), ultimately submitting to Allah’s sovereign will (*Yaf’alu ma yurid*).
